What Azure Elastic SAN actually is
The three building blocks: SAN, volume groups and volumes
How shared performance changes the design
Where Elastic SAN fits and where it doesn't

takeaways: Azure Elastic SAN pools high-performance block storage so that volumes share IOPS and throughput instead of each VM disk being sized for its own worst-case peak.
A SAN is organized into volume groups, which hold network and access rules, and volumes, which connect to workloads over iSCSI and whose performance scales with their size.

Elastic SAN fits groups of SQL Server databases, clustered workloads, Azure VMware Solution and supported Kubernetes designs whose peaks do not overlap, while small or isolation-sensitive workloads are often better on managed disks.
hook: As Azure environments grow, per-VM managed disks lead to paying for idle performance while busy workloads hit limits. This episode helps cloud architects and database teams understand Azure Elastic SAN, its building blocks and shared performance model, and decide when pooled block storage beats managed disks.
